newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares close slightly lower, seen easy.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares close slightly lower, seen easy.

text.p: Share prices drifted lower at the Bombay and National bourses on Friday with fewer participants ahead of the weekend, brokers said.
"It was a dull day," said one dealer at a foreign broking firm. "People are watching political developments."
He said players kept to the sidelines in anticipation of a long-awaited police report on a bribery scandal involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The 30-stock Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 2.29 points lower at a provisional 3,347.48, after sliding to 3,339.44.
The 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index slipped 1.57 points to a provisional 976.43.
The 500-stock CRISIL index shed 2.43 points to 656.50.
Traders said activity was heavy in bank stocks like SBI, OBC and Bank of Rajasthan, ahead of SBI's $400 million Euroissue and domestic offers by several other state-run banks.
SBI closed up 0.10 rupees at 263.55 in provisional volume of over 22.1 million shares on the NSE. The share gained 0.25 to 263.25 on the BSE with over 5.4 million shares traded.
OBC shed 0.55 rupees to 69.30 and Bank of Rajasthan 0.65 to 143.60 on the NSE.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were selectively active, traders said.
"The FIIs were looking for offers," one trader said. "Some funds were sellers."
ACC fell 19 rupees to 1,861.75, TELCO 7.75 to 455, Tata Power 4.25 to 137.25, Indian Hotel 18.50 to 739.50 and Grasim 3.75 to 418.50.
Bajaj Auto gained 8.50 rupees to 989, ITC 2.25 to 295, Hindalco 13.25 to 700 and Arvind Mills 2.50 to 125.25.
